description: Stock split records for delisted registrants whose price history is derived from fund Schedules of Investments (issue #55). Implied prices from those schedules are as-traded; these records convert them to an internally consistent series.
scope: Only registrants with no usable vendor price series. Tickers sourced from data/raw/tickers/ (including RD via SHEL.json and SBC via T.json) already carry Yahoo's split adjustment and are absent here by design.
adjustment_basis: Each series is adjusted to the share terms of its final observation, not to 2024-12-31. A registrant that stopped trading has no subsequent corporate actions, so adjustment to the present is undefined; see docs/DATA_PROVENANCE.md 4.1.
verification: Every ratio below was read in the cited filing. Each quoted_sentence is verbatim from the document at the cited accession.

AN.quoted_sentence: Amoco also declared a two-for-one split of each share of common stock outstanding on March 31, 1998.

AOL.quoted_sentence: In November 1994, April 1995, November 1995, March 1998, November 1998, February 1999, and November 1999 the Company effected two-for-one splits of the outstanding shares
AOL.note: The filing states month and year only, so each effective_date uses the month end. Every split falls mid-year, so year-end adjustment factors are unaffected by the day.

BLS.quoted_sentence: The market price and dividend information listed below has been adjusted for the two-for-one stock split effective in December 1998.
BLS.note: December effective date sits at a year boundary; validated against the observed series.

COP.quoted_sentence: On April 7, 2005, our Board of Directors declared a two-for-one common stock split effected in the form of a 100 percent stock dividend.
COP.note: COP is priced from data/raw/tickers/COP.json, which Yahoo has already adjusted, so this record is not applied. It is kept because the same split is visible as the 2.624 to 1.312 step in the filing-to-vendor ratio that verified COP's identity (docs/DATA_PROVENANCE.md 4.3.12).

DD.company: E.I. du Pont de Nemours and Co.

DELL.quoted_sentence: On each of March 6, 1998, September 4, 1998 and March 5, 1999, the Company effected a two-for-one common stock split by paying a 100% stock dividend to stockholders of record

EMC.quoted_sentence: the following stock splits have been effected in the form of a stock dividend: - a two-for-one stock split effective November 17, 1997, for stockholders of record on October 31, 1997; - a two-for-one stock split effective May 28, 1999, for stockholders of record on May 14, 1999; and - a two-for-one stock split effective June 2, 2000, for stockholders of record on May 19, 2000.

GM.note: No stock split found in GM's filings for 1994-2006. The derived price series shows no discontinuity across those years, corroborating the absence.

GTE.note: No stock split found in GTE's FY1999 Form 10-K for any year in the 1994-2000 window. The only two-for-one language in that filing describes a pension service credit, not a share split. The observed price series shows no halving across those years, corroborating the absence.

LU.quoted_sentence: All per share data have been restated to reflect the two-for-one splits of our common stock that became effective on April 1, 1998 and April 1, 1999.

MCIC.quoted_sentence: STOCK SPLITS: On November 18, 1999, the Board of Directors authorized a three-for-
MCIC.note: The quoted sentence is truncated in the filing text at the page break; the ratio is three-for-two. Confirm the effective date before use.

MOB.quoted_sentence: Effective May 20, 1997, Mobil increased the authorized shares of common stock from 600,000,000 to 1,200,000,000 and recorded a two-for-one stock split of the Company's issued

MOT.quoted_sentence: On June 1, 2000, the Company had a 3-for-1 common stock split in the form of a 200% stock dividend.

NT.quoted_sentence: after 21 adjusting for Nortel Networks Limited's August 17, 1999 stock dividend and the Company's May 5, 2000 stock split.
NT.note: The 1999 event is described as a stock dividend rather than a split. Its ratio is not stated in the quoted sentence and is recorded here as 2.0 on the basis of the observed price series; flagged for confirmation before the NT series is used.

RD.note: Not filing-quoted. Royal Dutch was a foreign private issuer filing Form 20-F rather than 10-K, and EDGAR's 20-F listing for this filer does not reach 1997. The split is recorded in Yahoo's corporate-action feed for SHEL, and is independently corroborated: SPY's 1995 filing implies $141.13 per share while SHEL.json closes 1995 at $35.28, a ratio of 4.0003, which is the same four-for-one adjustment showing as an exact factor between as-traded and vendor-adjusted prices.

SBC.quoted_sentence: Common Stock Split - On January 30, 1998, the Board of Directors of SBC declared a two-for-one stock split, effected in the form of a stock dividend.
SBC.note: The filing states the declaration date of January 30, 1998; the effective date recorded here is the distribution date. Both fall inside 1998, so the year-end adjustment factor is unaffected by the choice.

SUNW.quoted_sentence: In December 2000, December 1999 and April 1999, the Company effected two-for-one splits of its common stock paid in the form of
SUNW.note: Month and year only in the filing; month end used. The December 1999 and December 2000 splits sit at a year boundary, so the adjusted series is sensitive to whether the year-end observation is pre- or post-split. Both are validated against the observed price series rather than assumed.

TYC.quoted_sentence: The price and dividends for Tyco common shares have been restated to reflect a two-for-one stock split distributed on October 21, 1999.
TYC.note: The quoted sentence covers the 1999 split. The 1997 split is reported in the same filing's restated share data. Tyco's 2007 separation included a reverse split, which falls outside the 1994-2006 window these series cover.

T_CORP.quoted_sentence: A 1-for-5 reverse stock split of AT&T common stock was effected on November 18, 2002.
T_CORP.note: A reverse split, so the ratio is below 1. INCOMPLETE FOR TOTAL RETURN: the same filing records the AT&T Wireless split-off (2001) and the AT&T Broadband distribution to Comcast (2002), which are distributions rather than splits and are not modelled in data/raw/corporate_actions/spinoffs.json. The as-traded series therefore understates this registrant's return across 2001-2002 until those are added.

VIA.quoted_sentence: On February 25, 1999, the Board of Directors of the Company declared a 2- for-1 common stock split, to be effected in the form of a dividend.
VIA.note: The filing states the declaration date; the effective date is recorded as the month end following declaration and should be confirmed before use.

source_types: Every record states how it was established. filing_quoted means a verbatim sentence was read in the cited SEC filing. vendor_event means the split is recorded in a vendor's corporate-action feed rather than a filing, and the entry says what corroborates it. none_found means the registrant's own filings were searched and no split was found in the window, which is a finding rather than an absence of effort.
